ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a six-membered carbon ring structure, with a negative sign marked inside the ring, indicating that one CH on the ring carries a negative charge; the right side and lower side of the ring are each connected to one NO2 substituent; the tetravalent carbon at the top of the ring is simultaneously connected to a sulfonyl group SO2, a sulfur-containing side chain S-CH2-CO2H, and the two adjacent carbons of the ring. The sulfonyl group is further connected to NR1R2, and there is also a free H+ in the figure. There are multiple curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring these arrows. Reasoning: According to the specified writing method, NR1R2 is represented by the wildcard disubstituted amino group as *N(*), and connecting to the sulfonyl sulfur gives *N(*)S(=O)(=O). From sulfur connecting to the substituted carbon at the top of the ring and opening the ring is written as C1, and the thioacetic acid side chain on the same carbon is written as the branch (SCC(=O)O). When writing along the six-membered ring, write [CH-] at the position corresponding to the negative sign, add N(O)O branches at the two displayed nitro positions, finally close the ring, and write the free proton as a disconnected species .[H+]. Therefore the SMILES is *N(*)S(=O)(=O)C1(SCC(=O)O)C[CH-]C(N(O)O)CC1N(O)O.[H+].

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a static connectivity diagram and ignore all curved arrows as instructed. Start the SMILES at the dialkyl/diaryl amino substituent, representing NR1R2 as *N(*), then attach it to the sulfonyl sulfur: *N(*)S(=O)(=O). Continue from sulfur to the substituted top carbon of the six-membered ring and open the ring as C1. Add the branch from that same carbon for the thioacetic acid substituent, (SCC(=O)O). Traverse the ring in one consistent direction, placing the negatively charged CH where the minus sign is drawn and adding the two NO2 substituents at their displayed ring positions as N(O)O branches. Close the ring and append the separate proton as a disconnected species. This yields *N(*)S(=O)(=O)C1(SCC(=O)O)C[CH-]C(N(O)O)CC1N(O)O.[H+].
